summary: How the Roman Republic slid from the 509 BCE expulsion of its kings through land inequality, the murder of the Gracchi, gang warfare and civil war, until Augustus built riot police, secret police and a Praetorian Guard that later made and killed emperors.

evidence.note: Tarquin expelled and republic founded in 509 BCE; early constitution follows at length
long Tiberius Gracchus segment begins: birth, Numantia, land reform, murder
Tiberius negotiates the Numantia truce in northern Spain
public land seized by the rich and worked by slaves; dispossessed veterans
professional political street gangs of Clodius and Milo; daily assassinations
Marius and Sulla civil war, Sulla's proscriptions and dictatorship
Augustus founds the urban cohorts, the first standing police in Rome
frumentarii turned into imperial secret police and assassins
Praetorians auction the throne after Commodus; Septimius Severus replaces them (193 CE)

notes: No primary person, so roles empty. Covered span starts at the republic's founding, which gets ~10 minutes; end set at 193 CE (Praetorian auction and Severus), the last period with real airtime; a brief quote reaching Diocletian and Julian was left out. Lucretia's rape and suicide get ~3 minutes but not a detailed account, so no warning. Modern US comparisons are commentary, not covered years.
